about: Class levels. Each rule has a value, a source (jay, research or assumption) and a plain note. The generator never uses an exercise above the class level.

bodyPartsLifted.text: Counts each leg held in the air with nothing under it, plus one if the whole torso is held up with nothing under it (like a teaser). Legs resting in straps, arms in straps, and a small head and shoulders curl (HNS) are not counted.

unilateral.text: One arm or one leg works on its own, or one leg carries the body weight. Doing a stretch one side at a time is not counted.

skills.text: Exercises can carry the tags coordination (arms and legs doing different things, or a tricky pattern), balance (an unstable surface, one leg, or balancing on the sit bones) and stability (holding the body still against a load, like planks and kneeling on the carriage).

summary.value: Foundations. Everything stays supported, both sides work together, no chair.

maxBodyPartsLifted.note: Some body part always on the ground. Nothing lifts.

allowLowerLevel.note: Exercises at the class level or below, never above.

avoidSkills.note: No tricky moves at Level 1. Exercises tagged coordination or balance are never used.

transitionFactor.note: Follows Jay: no tricky transitions at Level 1, so the builder works hard to keep clients in one position.

guidance.value: Foundation work. Build the challenge through reps, range, springs, positioning and sequencing, not tricky moves or transitions.

summary.value: One body part can lift. Single leg and single arm work allowed. A little chair.

maxBodyPartsLifted.note: One body part can lift, like one leg in tabletop.

maxChairMinutes.note: Jay said limited chair. Read as up to 12 minutes and Level 1.5 chair exercises only.

allowLowerLevel.note: Exercises at the class level or below, never above.

preferSkills.note: Level 1.5 adds coordination, balance and stability challenges, so the builder leans toward them.

transitionFactor.note: Follows Jay: more interesting transitions at Level 1.5, so position changes cost little.

guidance.value: Adds coordination, balance and stability challenges, intermediate progressions and more interesting transitions.

summary.value: Everything can lift. Full chair. Classic intermediate repertoire.

maxChairMinutes.note: Advanced chair allowed. No time limit.

allowInversions.note: Short spine and similar are standard at this level. Older clients still never get them.

allowLowerLevel.note: Exercises at the class level or below, never above.

guidance.value: Classic intermediate repertoire. Everything can lift.

summary.value: Strong intermediate. Everything can lift. Longer holds and harder variations.

maxChairMinutes.note: Advanced chair allowed. No time limit.

allowInversions.note: Older clients still never get them.

allowLowerLevel.note: Exercises at the class level or below, never above.

guidance.value: Strong intermediate. Longer holds and harder variations.

gentlerNote.value: Levels follow common contemporary studio standards, then each exercise was placed half a level higher when in doubt, because Jay's clients skew older.
